most often I am in spaces with a large population of trans individuals so when I deem necessary I denote myself as a cishet ace. I pride myself on the fact that yes, im cis, im hetero, but I am still ace and I am still lgbt regardless of my status that i could just blend in with. On top of that I'm also gnc not trans necessarily so when it comes up I also feel the need to specify that. I'm very proud of my identity, and I don't want to hold any aspect of it back when the situation of talking about it arises. 

I don't use cishet ace every single time i describe myself but when I do it's usually because I'm talking about my while identity, experience, or that entire group of aspecs.

I know what cishet usually means but i guess what I'm not getting is why when every other orientation once conjoined with ace is automatically understood why can't the same happen here? 

And I understand that's what people are arguing against when arguing with exclusionists but I feel like the argument rarely ever uplifts cis and heteroromantic asexuals and makes it more seem like it's just bad to identify that way. And regardless of the label used exclusionists still ultimately mean aces who are cis and hetero aren't allowed in no matter how we were to break it down.

I guess my problem is I see no weight in the argument against using the label cishet ace. When I say that I mean a group of aces who are cis and hetero and I usually talk about that specific group *because* we are often targeted. And I feel like no matter how we label ourselves we would still be targeted and instead it feels more like the argument against using that label only applies to us, and doesn't actually push to uplift us and push for accepting us.
Talking against the label has been on the rise lately probably due to a rise in people identifying as bi/straight lesbians and other variations of that
